source: Pathfinder 1st Edition special materials (Core Rulebook, Ultimate Equipment) and the skymetals (Pathfinder Campaign Setting), with fuels, fluxes, quenchants and fittings authored for the forge chains.
note: Tier follows the worldclass ladder: common/uncommon/rare/exotic/legendary. The forge reads `pieces`, `weapon`, `armour`, `working` and `quench_mark` through rules/materials.py (docs/blacksmithing-contracts.md §3); effects marked "book": true are printed PF1e rules, applied from the main piece only and never scaled, and every other number is a house modifier for the owner's review (docs/blacksmithing-review.md). `effects` is the pre-revamp flat list that rules/blacksmith.py still reads until its bench moves to the new fields. `weight_factor` is the old weight multiplier the same reader uses. `source` is how a smith gets it: mined, bought, harvested or monster.

materials.name: Iron Ore
materials.text: Red-brown haematite, the commonest ore worth carting. It smelts to iron, and assaying a lump tells you what iron will do; the melt is wide and patient.

materials.name: Bog Iron
materials.text: Lumps of ore raked out of marsh beds. Cheap and everywhere, and it smelts to soft wrought iron, but full of slag: work from it cannot reach its best until the melt is fluxed clean or the bar is folded.

effects.target: damage
effects.note: slag-brittle: on work smelted from unfluxed bog iron

materials.name: Copper Ore
materials.text: Green malachite and blue azurite, smelting quickly to copper, the first metal anyone ever worked. Soft alone; the better half of bronze.

materials.name: Tin Ore
materials.text: Heavy black cassiterite from stream gravels. It smelts fast to tin, worth more than its weight suggests: without tin there is no bronze.

materials.name: Lead Ore
materials.text: Glittering cubic galena, so heavy a sack of it staggers a mule. Smelts low and easy to lead, and a botched melt costs nothing but the fire.

materials.name: Calamine
materials.text: Dull zinc earth. It smelts to zinc only in a tight band of heat before the metal boils off; most smiths heap it in with copper and take brass instead.

materials.name: Cinnabar Ore
materials.text: Blood-red mercury ore. Roasting it drives off quicksilver as an invisible vapour, so assaying it is dangerous, and the roast must be caught in a narrow band or the metal is lost to the air.

effects.target: fort
effects.note: roasting fumes, to whoever works it unmasked

materials.name: Silver Ore
materials.text: Dark sulphide ore threaded with native wire silver. It smelts to silver carrying dross that a bone-ash cupel or a fold has to take out.

materials.name: Gold Ore
materials.text: Quartz veined with visible gold, or dust panned from river gravel. It smelts clean to gold, and a smelt of it is very hard to spoil.

materials.name: Nickel Ore
materials.text: Kupfernickel, 'devil's copper', named by miners it disappointed. It gives no metal a smith can forge alone; it feeds an alloy, where it makes a weld take more easily, after a dirty and finicky smelt.

materials.name: Cold Iron Ore
materials.text: Iron mined deep underground, never touched by the sun. It smelts to cold iron only at a lower heat than common iron, in a narrow band that forgives no shortcuts.

effects.target: Smelts to cold iron: bypasses the damage reduction of demons and fey

materials.name: Platinum Ore
materials.text: Grey grains heavier than gold that shrug off every acid in the alchemist's cabinet. It smelts to platinum only at furnace heat few smithies reach, and comes out pure when it does.

materials.name: Mithral Ore
materials.text: Silvery ore light enough to surprise the hand that lifts it. It smelts to mithral, and the book says it is worked like steel: the heat is forgiving.

materials.name: Adamantine Ore
materials.text: Night-black metal found only in the hearts of fallen stars and the deepest delvings. It smelts to adamantine in a narrow band of white heat that only a rare fuel reaches.

materials.name: Abysium Ore
materials.text: A skymetal ore that glows blue-green in the dark and warms the hand that holds it. It smelts to abysium, and it sickens whoever carries it: assaying it is genuinely dangerous.

effects.target: fort
effects.note: each day spent carrying or working it unshielded

materials.name: Djezet Seep
materials.text: Rust-red skymetal that is liquid at every temperature, collected drop by drop where it seeps from volcanic rock. Carried in wax-stoppered vials; nothing a smith does to it can ruin it.

materials.name: Inubrix Ore
materials.text: The ghost iron. Seams of it are found threaded through iron deposits they have visibly sunk through. It smelts to inubrix, only slightly less malleable than lead.

materials.name: Noqual Ore
materials.text: Pale green skymetal crystal, found in crater rims. Detect magic slides off a nugget of it as though there were nothing there. It smelts to noqual, which the book says is worked as iron.

materials.name: Siccatite Ore
materials.text: A skymetal that comes out of the ground either searing hot or freezing cold and never changes its mind. It smelts to siccatite, and assaying it burns.

effects.note: hot ore, to a bare hand each round it is held; cold ore deals the same in cold

materials.name: Horacalcum Ore
materials.text: The rarest skymetal: a dull coppery ore around which time runs a half-step slow. It smelts to horacalcum in the narrowest band of any ore.

materials.name: Iron
materials.text: Bar iron, the smith's daily bread, and heavy with it. An iron head hits harder and swings slower, and iron plate turns more blows and stiffens the wearer; either way the piece is harder to break. Its heat band is wide and forgiving.

materials.name: Wrought Iron
materials.text: Iron worked soft and fibrous, with the slag hammered into threads. It bends before it breaks: a wrought head is tough and hard to wrest away but cuts softly, and wrought mail moves with the wearer at the cost of hardness. Very hard to ruin at the anvil.

materials.name: Bismuth
materials.text: A brittle white metal that cools into staircase crystals sheened like oil on water. Useless for an edge and fills no piece; alloyers melt it in for pours that must run thin, and it helps a weld take.

materials.name: Copper
materials.text: Warm red metal that works cold and greens with age. A copper head swings true and will not shatter, but cuts softly; copper armour is supple and tough and turns fewer blows, with the book's hardness of 9. In the book a copper weapon is fragile, which this app does not yet model.

armour.note: primitive bronze, copper or tin armour: hardness 9

materials.name: Tin
materials.text: Soft grey metal that cries when bent. As fittings and fastenings it lightens the piece and lets a hand or a body move quicker, and it is the first thing to give. One part in ten turns copper into bronze.

materials.name: Lead
materials.text: Dense, dull and obedient: it melts over a candle and holds any shape. A lead pommel or counterweight puts weight behind a blow and drags the swing; a lead lining deadens blows and the wearer pays for it in weight. The lining that stops scrying is its own treatment.

effects.target: A lead lining blocks detect spells and scrying through the lined surface

materials.name: Zinc
materials.text: Bluish-white and brittle, boiling away out of any careless melt. It fills no piece; it is alloying stock, married to copper to make brass.

materials.name: Silver
materials.text: The moon's metal, too soft to hold an edge alone. Silver fittings make a weapon bite harder and truer against shapechangers, and silver fastenings let armour move freely; both are softer than steel. A weapon that strikes as silver is the alchemical plating treatment.

effects.target: Plated over steel it bypasses the damage reduction of lycanthropes and some devils

materials.name: Gold
materials.text: Heavy, incorruptible and useless in a fight, exactly as the book prints it: solid gold cuts softer, guards worse, weighs half again and breaks easily. What it does is announce the owner, and people listen. The kindest metal at the anvil.

weapon.note: solid gold weapon, minimum 1
half the base hardness
solid gold

armour.note: solid gold armour
the book's +2 check penalty
hardness 5
solid gold

materials.name: Platinum
materials.text: White metal that no acid touches and no common furnace melts. A platinum head is dense enough to hit very hard and drags the swing; platinum armour shrugs off acid and turns blows, and is very heavy.

materials.name: Cold Iron
materials.text: Iron mined deep and forged at low heat, never allowed to forget the dark it came from. A cold iron head strikes as cold iron, through the defences of demons and fey, and swings truer against the fey; cold iron armour steadies the wearer's will. Forged low, it is softer than common iron, and its heat window is narrow.

effects.target: Bypasses the damage reduction of demons and fey (DR/cold iron)
Costs double the forge-time and coin: cold iron forgives no reworking

materials.name: Star Iron
materials.text: Meteoric iron, sky-fallen and already smelted by its landing, which makes it quick to work and full of stony inclusions. A star-iron head strikes as cold iron and hits hard but chips; star-iron plate is hard and stiff. A house metal with no book behind it.

effects.target: Counts as cold iron against damage reduction

materials.name: Viridium
materials.text: A dull green volcanic glass, knapped rather than forged, though smiths shelve it with the metals. Only a piercing or slashing head: every hit risks leprosy (Fortitude DC 12), a critical leaves a sliver of greenblood oil (DC 13), and whoever carries it saves against the leprosy each day unless the blade sleeps in lead. Half as hard as steel, and fragile in the book.

effects.target: fort
effects.note: leprosy, on any wound from a viridium edge

weapon.note: leprosy: onset 2d4 weeks, 1/week, cured by 2 consecutive saves; oozes, plants and outsiders are immune
a fragment breaks off as greenblood oil: 1/round for 4 rounds
leprosy, saved every 24 hours, unless kept extradimensional or in a lead-lined scabbard
half hardness

materials.name: Mithral
materials.text: Truesilver: harder than steel at half the weight. A mithral head strikes as silver and is quick in the hand but light behind the blow. Mithral armour is the book's: half weight, a lighter check penalty, two more points of Dexterity, less spell failure, and it moves one class lighter, for movement and never for proficiency. Its plates are thinner than steel's. Worked like steel, forgivingly.

effects.target: Half weight; armour counts one category lighter for movement (not for proficiency)
Armour: maximum Dexterity bonus +2, armour check penalty 3 lighter, spell failure 10% lower; a weapon counts as silver

armour.note: armour check penalty 3 lighter, never above 0
for movement only, never for proficiency

materials.name: Adamantine
materials.text: The unbreakable night-black metal of fallen stars, hardness 20. An adamantine head strikes as adamantine, through hardness below 20, and hits harder, though it is heavier than steel. Adamantine armour gives the book's damage reduction of 1, 2 or 3 by weight and turns blows, but it does not flex.

effects.target: A weapon of it ignores hardness less than 20 when sundering or striking objects, and never loses its masterwork edge to wear

effects.note: armour: DR 3/— in heavy, 2/— in medium, 1/— in light

weapon.note: ignores hardness below 20

materials.name: Abysium
materials.text: Feverstone: a skymetal that glows like a candle and works as steel. Its weapons bite and its armour turns blows better than steel, and it sickens whoever carries it, with no save, until 1d4 hours after it is put down. Assaying it is genuinely dangerous.

effects.target: sickened
effects.note: while carried and for 1d4 hours after; a poison effect, no save

effects.target: Glows: sheds light as a candle, and cannot be hidden from creatures that see it

weapon.note: while carried and for 1d4 hours after; a poison effect, no save

armour.note: while carried and for 1d4 hours after; a poison effect, no save

materials.name: Djezet
materials.text: The quickmetal: rust-red and liquid at every temperature. It fills no piece; the book makes it useless for metal objects except alloys, and at the crucible it is the kindest of the skymetals. Its spell-quickening use is a spellcaster's, not a smith's.

effects.target: Veined through a piece it quickens spellcasting focused through it; alone it never holds a shape

materials.name: Inubrix
materials.text: Ghost iron, the softest of the skymetals. An inubrix head is always broken in the book, deals damage as a size smaller and cannot harm iron or steel, but passes through iron and steel armour as if it were not there; here it swings truer against a metal-armoured foe. Poor for armour, so it fills no armour piece.

effects.target: Ignores armour and shield bonuses from iron or steel, but is always broken, deals damage as one size smaller and cannot damage iron or steel

weapon.note: always broken
always broken; and damage as one size smaller
hardness 5
10 hit points per inch
house approximation of the book's 'ignores armour and shield bonuses from iron or steel'

materials.name: Noqual
materials.text: Pale green and crystalline, and magic slides off it. Noqual is half weight; its weapons bite constructs and made undead harder, and its armour moves a class lighter and wards its wearer against spells, at a fifth more spell failure for any caster. Any magic item made with it costs 5,000 gp more to enchant. Worked as iron, but assaying it is dangerous: magic recoils from it, and whatever spells and wards the assayer carries go quiet for a few moments (a house rule).

effects.target: Half weight; armour: +2 resistance on saves against spells, +20% spell failure for all casting, one category lighter; any magic item made with it costs 5,000 gp more

weapon.note: constructs made by feats or spells
undead made by feats or spells

armour.note: for all spellcasting, not only arcane

assay_danger.note: House rule (the owner, 2026-10-04): magic recoils. Assaying a sliver suppresses the assayer's active magical effects, buffs and wards, for 1d4 rounds.

materials.name: Siccatite
materials.text: The skymetal of extremes; this is the hot kind. A siccatite head brands what it hits for a point of fire and burns its wielder a point each round of combat. Siccatite armour burns its wearer and anyone who grapples them, and keeps the cold off. Assaying it burns.

effects.note: hot siccatite, each round of bare contact — including the wielder's ungloved grip
frigid siccatite, each round of bare contact

weapon.note: hot siccatite; cold siccatite deals cold
to the wielder, each round of combat

armour.note: to the wearer, each round
to whoever grapples the wearer, each round
hot siccatite armour; cold siccatite gives fire resistance 5 instead

materials.name: Horacalcum
materials.text: The rarest skymetal, a dull coppery gold around which time runs slow. A horacalcum blade gives the book's +1 on the attack and puts its bearer ahead in the fight, though it lands lightly. Horacalcum armour quickens the wearer by its weight, +1 to +3 initiative, and sits stiffly.

effects.target: attack
effects.note: a horacalcum weapon; armour instead gives +1/+2/+3 initiative by weight

weapon.note: not ammunition

materials.name: Steel
materials.text: Iron with carbon taken into itself in the fire. A steel head swings true and holds its hardness, and is less forgiving of a hard knock than iron; steel plate turns blows and is hard, and binds the wearer a little. The trade's whole ladder of quench, temper and hone exists because steel answers to it.

materials.name: Bronze
materials.text: Copper and tin, the metal that named an age. A bronze head swings true and is tough but softer than steel; bronze armour turns blows, has the book's hardness of 9, and is heavy. Casts beautifully. In the book bronze weapons are fragile, which this app does not yet model.

armour.note: primitive bronze armour: hardness 9

materials.name: Brass
materials.text: Copper and zinc, gold's honest cousin. Brass fittings hold a blade in the hand and shine without a servant, and brass fastenings move easily; it is softer than steel. Easy to work and file.

materials.name: Pewter
materials.text: Tin stiffened with a little copper and less honesty. Pewter buckles and fittings are light and cheap and the first thing to break.

materials.name: Electrum
materials.text: Gold and silver as nature sometimes pours them together, pale and moonish. Electrum fittings impress, and carry enough silver to bite a shapechanger harder; fastenings of it impress and flex. Soft, and a pleasure to work.

materials.name: Bell Bronze
materials.text: Bronze rich in tin, brittle as glass and voiced like an angel. Fittings of it ring on every blow, which unsettles whoever hears them; it is hard and it cracks. Casts easily.

effects.target: Rings when struck: a signal audible far beyond shouting distance

materials.name: High-Carbon Steel
materials.text: Steel fed carbon to the edge of temper's patience. A head of it cuts deeper and holds its hardness, and plate of it turns more blows, but both shatter sooner. The quench is narrow and brine cracks it on a miss.

effects.target: Holds its sharpness: an edge of it needs honing half as often

materials.name: Pattern Steel
materials.text: Billets of hard and soft steel folded and welded until the blade carries water-marks. Spring and edge in one bar: it cuts deep and survives what snaps a plain blade, and is a little softer for the spring. Masterwork costs it no extra difficulty, in a narrow heat window.

effects.target: The watered pattern marks folded work: spring where a plain blade would snap

materials.name: Nexavaran Steel
materials.text: Cold iron drawn out with a measure of common steel, the compromise metal of frontier fey-hunters. A head of it strikes as cold iron, as the book says, and cuts well but is softer; armour of it steadies the will and is stiff.

effects.target: Counts as cold iron against damage reduction, at 1.5 times common cost rather than double

materials.name: Elysian Bronze
materials.text: Bronze alloyed with traces of celestial metal, first beaten out for heroes who hunted monsters. Its weapons bite magical beasts and monstrous humanoids harder, and after drawing blood from one swing truer against that kind for a day. Its armour gives damage reduction, 1 to 3 by weight, against their claws and fists. Softer than steel, and stiff as armour.

effects.target: damage
effects.note: against magical beasts and monstrous humanoids

weapon.note: multiplied on a critical hit
after it damages one, against that kind of creature for 24 hours

armour.note: only against their natural weapons and unarmed strikes
only against their natural weapons and unarmed strikes
only against their natural weapons and unarmed strikes

materials.name: Living Steel
materials.text: Steel quickened by waters from trees that will not die: the book's hardness 15 and 35 hit points an inch. A living-steel weapon is hard to wrest away and its grain fights the hand; its armour turns blows and is stiff. In the book it mends 2 hit points a day and can break a weapon that rolls a 1 against it; neither is modelled yet.

effects.target: Repairs 2 hit points a day (1 if broken); a metal weapon that rolls a natural 1 against its armour saves DC 20 Fortitude or breaks

materials.name: Fire-Forged Steel
materials.text: Dwarven steel worked with channels that carry heat one way. Its armour gives the book's fire resistance 2, always, and turns blows but is stiff. Its weapons bite cold creatures harder and are tough but softer. The book's weapon rule, extra fire after it has sat in flame, is not modelled yet.

effects.target: fire
effects.note: armour, always

materials.name: Frost-Forged Steel
materials.text: The winter twin of fire-forged steel. Its armour gives the book's cold resistance 2, always, and turns blows but binds the wearer. Its weapons bite fire creatures harder and are tough but softer. The book's weapon rule, extra cold after it has been chilled, is not modelled yet.

effects.target: cold
effects.note: armour, always

materials.name: Singing Steel
materials.text: A pale gold and mithral alloy that chimes at a touch. Its weapons strike as alchemical silver, with silver's lighter cut; its armour moves a class lighter with a little less spell failure and check penalty. Both are less tough than steel, and both carry a performer's voice. In the book striking it speeds a bardic performance; here it lends Perform.

effects.target: damage
effects.note: counts as alchemical silver: slashing or piercing only

weapon.note: counts as alchemical silver: slashing or piercing only, minimum 1
20 hit points per inch

armour.note: 20 hit points per inch

materials.name: Wyrmsteel
materials.text: Adamantine folded over dragonfire coal and quenched in dragon's blood, an alloy more legend than recipe. Its weapons strike as adamantine and hit very hard, and are heavy; its armour keeps a dragon's indifference to flame and turns blows, and is stiff. A house metal with no book behind it.

effects.target: fire
effects.note: the metal's own dragon-nature, carried by armour of it

materials.name: Peat
materials.text: Cut from the bog and dried through a season. Burns low, slow and smoky: a forgiving fire for a field forge, but it runs sulfurous and leaves the work slaggy.

materials.name: Coal
materials.text: Black seam-rock that burns hotter and longer than wood, so work goes faster, but raw coal is sulfurous and a careless heat leaves the iron hot-short.

materials.name: Charcoal
materials.text: Wood burned slow under turf until only the burning part is left. Clean, forgiving heat that adds nothing to the melt but temperature, which is exactly what a smith wants.

materials.name: Coke
materials.text: Coal baked in an airless oven until its smoke and sulphur are driven off. Burns hotter and cleaner than coal, so the work goes quickly, in a tighter heat band.

materials.name: Bone Char
materials.text: Charred bone, packed around iron to feed carbon into the surface. The fuel of case-hardening: a clean heat that lifts work to masterwork without extra difficulty, in a narrow band.

materials.name: Dwarven Hearthcoal
materials.text: Coal from seams the dwarves keep secret, dense as ore and slow as grudges. One scuttle burns a day and a night at forging heat: clean, steady and quick to work over.

materials.name: Dragonfire Coal
materials.text: Coal from seams a dragon once slept over. It burns white, hot enough to melt the skymetals, fast and in a narrow band, and sulfurous; it does not care whether the smith's beard is in the way.

materials.name: Salamander Cinder
materials.text: Embers raked from a slain salamander's own hearth-flesh. They burn without fuel for a month, so the work is quick and a bad blow can be reheated and saved, in a narrow band.

effects.note: to bare skin within reach of the cinders, each round

materials.name: Efreet Brand
materials.text: A brand from a bonfire on the Plane of Fire, carried home still burning. Forge-fire from it burns any colour the smith asks: the widest heat band there is, and very hard to spoil a piece over.

materials.name: Phoenix Ash Ember
materials.text: An ember from the pyre of a phoenix, which relights itself by morning however it is put out. Nothing forged over it is ruined by a bad blow, the check is rolled twice, and masterwork costs no extra difficulty.

materials.name: Limestone Flux
materials.text: Crushed grey stone thrown into the melt, where it gathers the slag and floats it off the good metal. The cheapest honest flux: it cleans a smelt and makes it easier.

materials.name: Silica Sand
materials.text: Clean white sand for the forge-weld: it melts to glass and keeps the air off the joint. Helps folding and strengthening, cleans a little slag, and wants a precise heat.

materials.name: Potash
materials.text: Wood ash leached and boiled down to a white salt. An old fireside flux for small work and soldering: welds come easier and a slip spoils nothing.

materials.name: Borax
materials.text: White crystal from dry lake beds, the wandering smith's flux: it melts low, widens the weld's heat band, and leaves a weld clean enough for masterwork at no extra difficulty.

materials.name: Bone Ash
materials.text: Calcined bone, the assayer's flux. It soaks base metal away and leaves silver and gold sitting proud: it cleans a smelt and the check is rolled twice, in a narrow heat.

materials.name: Crushed Quartz
materials.text: Clear crystal ground fine, for melts that must run glassy. Finicky, with a narrow heat, and worth it: fine work reaches masterwork at no extra difficulty and welds come easier.

materials.name: Consecrated Flux
materials.text: Chalk blessed at a temple altar and ground with silver dust. In the melt it cleans thoroughly and steadies the smith's hand. A flux leaves no mark on the finished work; for a blessed edge, quench in holy water or anoint it.

materials.name: Abyssal Salt
materials.text: Salt scraped from the shores of a lake in the Abyss. It strips a melt cleaner and faster than any earthly flux, and assaying it is dangerous: holy water hisses on it.

materials.name: Stardust Flux
materials.text: Glittering dust gathered where a star fell, sold by the pinch. It makes any weld take, steadies the check and costs masterwork nothing extra; the old smiths say it alone persuades the skymetals to mingle.

materials.name: Water
materials.text: The oldest bath, always to hand. Quenches fast and hard, leaving the piece a point harder, in a narrow window that cracks a careless blade.

materials.name: Quenching Brine
materials.text: Salt water bites faster than sweet. It leaves the hardest skin of the common baths, and the narrowest window, and it can leave a careless blade brittle.

materials.name: Quenching Oil
materials.text: Rendered fat or seed oil, the gentle bath. Slower than water and kinder: the piece comes out tougher rather than harder, and a bad quench ruins nothing.

materials.name: Whale Oil
materials.text: The finest quenching oil money buys, even-tempered from first plunge to last. Leaves the piece tougher, and the quench is forgiving and sure.

materials.name: Glacier Melt
materials.text: Water from ice older than the kingdom. A blade quenched in it keeps a little winter: its bearer shrugs off a point of cold. A sharp, clean quench.

materials.name: Mercury Bath
materials.text: Quicksilver quenches with unearthly evenness, leaving the piece a point harder, and gives off a vapour that steals wits: assaying it is dangerous.

effects.target: fort
effects.note: the hot vapour, each quench performed without wind or mask

materials.name: Blessed Water
materials.text: Holy water enough to quench in, which is a conversation with the temple first. Steel quenched in it bites the undead a little harder. It does not make the blade good-aligned: in the book that needs magic, and a quench is not magic.

effects.target: damage
effects.note: against undead

materials.name: Troll Blood
materials.text: Blood drawn from a troll and kept warm, because it does not accept being dead. What it hardens heals its bearer: fast healing 1 for a minute after the first wound each day.

effects.note: once a day, after the first wound

materials.name: Wyvern Blood
materials.text: Envenomed blood from a wyvern's tail-stock. A blade quenched in it carries the sting into its first wound each day: Fortitude DC 17 or 1d4 Constitution. Assaying it is dangerous.

effects.target: fort
effects.note: the venom lingers in the first telling wound the finished blade deals

quench_mark.note: wyvern venom, in the first wound the blade deals each day

materials.name: Dragon Blood
materials.text: Blood of a true dragon, which quenches steel without ever quite going cold. The piece takes a shadow of the donor's element: its bearer resists 2 fire from a red dragon's blood.

effects.target: fire
effects.note: armour quenched in a fire dragon's blood; other lineages lend their own element

quench_mark.note: a fire dragon's blood; other lineages lend their own element

materials.name: Styx Water
materials.text: Water from the river of forgetting, carried in horn. A blade quenched in it bites outsiders harder and dulls its bearer's will; the smith works fast and tries not to breathe the steam.

effects.target: damage
effects.note: against outsiders; the bearer takes -1 on Will saves

effects.target: damage
will

materials.name: Ash Haft
materials.text: Straight-grained ash, the spear-wood. Springy in the hand, so the weapon swings truer and is harder to wrest away, though wood is weaker than steel.

materials.name: Oak Haft
materials.text: Heavy, stiff and stubborn: the right wood under an axe or maul that leads with weight. It hits harder and lasts, and drags the swing.

materials.name: Bone Grip
materials.text: Scales of polished bone riveted to the tang. Hard-wearing and sure against a disarm, and slick in a sweating hand.

materials.name: Leather Grip
materials.text: Wet-wrapped leather that dries to the shape of the hand. As a grip it holds true and hard to wrest away; as a lining it pads blows and eases movement at the cost of weight.

materials.name: Cord-Wrapped Grip
materials.text: Waxed cord laid in tight courses over the tang. Grips wet or dry, which helps both the swing and a trip or disarm, and wears through; a field repair needs only more cord.

materials.name: Brass Guard
materials.text: A cast brass crossguard or basket, bright and forgiving to file. It hardens the hilt and turns a disarming blade, and cast brass cracks before forged steel would.

materials.name: Steel Crossguard
materials.text: Plain forged steel between hand and harm. It turns a disarm and outlasts the grip, and adds weight. Nothing about it is clever, which is why it works.

materials.name: Wire-Wrapped Grip
materials.text: Twisted silver or steel wire laid over leather, the duellist's grip: it does not shift in the hand, so the blade swings true and is hard to take away. Fiddly to lay, and softer than a solid grip.

effects.target: cmd
effects.note: against being disarmed of the fitted weapon

weapon.note: the duellist's grip, against being disarmed

materials.name: Sharkskin Grip
materials.text: Ray or shark hide, rough as a file in one direction. It never slips, wet, bloody or otherwise, so the swing and the grab are both surer; a hide grip is softer than bone.

materials.name: Mammoth Ivory Grip
materials.text: Ancient ivory dug from the tundra, dense and cool. It outlasts the blade and impresses anyone who sees it, and it is slick in the hand.

materials.name: Darkwood Haft
materials.text: Wood as dark as coffee and half the weight of oak. On a wholly wooden weapon the book halves its weight; as a haft under a metal head the book gives nothing, so here it is quick in the hand and light behind the blow.

effects.target: Half weight on a wholly wooden weapon (the book gives a haft alone no benefit)

weapon.note: only where the wood is the main piece: a wholly wooden weapon, as the book requires

materials.name: Ironwood Haft
materials.text: Wood worked by druidic rite until it answers as steel: as hard and tough, and heavier than plain wood. It is still wood in the eyes of oath and spell, and rust never touches it.

effects.target: Counts as wood for druidic oaths and spells that care, at the strength of steel

materials.name: Wyroot Haft
materials.text: Root-wood that refuses to finish dying. A confirmed critical through a wyroot haft gives its wielder a spark of life once a day, and the haft swings true but is weaker than ash. The book stores a point for ki or arcane pools, which the app does not have.

weapon.note: house approximation of the book's stored life point; gone at dusk

materials.name: Dragonhide Grip
materials.text: Red dragonhide, supple where scale meets scale. The grip shrugs off flame, so its wielder does too, and it holds the weapon fast, but the scale is slick under a swing. The book's dragonhide is for armour and shields.

effects.target: fire
effects.note: a red dragonhide grip, to its wielder

materials.name: Angelskin Binding
materials.text: Pale leather from a celestial's remains. Bound inside armour it steadies the wearer's will and turns blows, and anyone who learns what it is trusts them less. The book's angelskin dims an evil aura, which the app does not model.

materials.name: Fiend Bone Core
materials.text: A rod of fiend's bone set down the spine of a haft. The weapon swings a half-thought ahead of its wielder, quick and true, and it whispers: the wielder's will weakens. Assaying it is dangerous.

materials.name: Bluing
materials.text: A controlled black-blue oxide raised over the steel. Rust has nowhere to start, so the piece lasts a little longer. Quick and forgiving to apply.

weapon.note: rust has nowhere to start

armour.note: rust has nowhere to start

materials.name: Oil Blackening
materials.text: The piece is heated and plunged in oil until it carries a dead-black skin. It throws no glint, which is worth a point of Stealth.

effects.target: stealth
effects.note: a blackened piece throws no glint

weapon.note: a blackened piece throws no glint

armour.note: a blackened piece throws no glint

materials.name: Acid Etching
materials.text: Wax resist and aqua fortis, biting a design or a maker's mark into the steel. A marked piece carries its provenance, worth a point of Diplomacy. The acid bites fast.

weapon.note: a maker's mark and provenance

armour.note: a maker's mark and provenance

materials.name: Cold Iron Blanching
materials.text: The book's weapon blanch: powdered cold iron melted over an edge in a round of flame. The weapon strikes as cold iron until it next hits, and then it is only steel again. One dose coats a weapon or ten arrows.

effects.target: Strikes as cold iron until the weapon next hits

weapon.note: weapon blanch: until the weapon next hits; one dose coats one weapon or 10 pieces of ammunition

materials.name: Ghost Salt Blanching
materials.text: A white alchemical crust worked over the striking surface. The weapon strikes as ghost touch: an incorporeal creature takes its full damage instead of half, until the weapon next hits.

effects.target: Deals full damage to incorporeal creatures until the weapon next hits

weapon.note: the book's full damage to incorporeal creatures until the weapon next hits

materials.name: Alchemical Silver Plating
materials.text: Silver alchemically bonded over a steel core. The weapon strikes as silver, through the defences of lycanthropes and devils, and a slashing or piercing edge loses a point of damage. The book forbids it on adamantine, cold iron and mithral.

effects.target: damage
effects.note: slashing or piercing only, minimum 1

effects.target: Strikes as silver; cannot be applied to adamantine, cold iron or mithral

weapon.note: slashing or piercing only, minimum 1

materials.name: Gold Gilding
materials.text: Gold leaf burnished onto the finished piece. It stops no blow; it announces the owner across a room, which is worth two points of Diplomacy.

materials.name: Lead Lining
materials.text: Sheet lead beaten into the inner faces of a helm or breastplate. Scrying stops at the lead: the wearer's will is a point harder to reach, and the armour a tenth heavier.

armour.note: against scrying and divination: a house stand-in for the lead's block

materials.name: Holy Anointing
materials.text: The finished work is oiled, censed and blessed at an altar. For its first battle after the rite it bites the undead harder; the rites do not last.

weapon.note: its first battle after the rite

materials.name: Adamantine Edging
materials.text: A ribbon of adamantine forge-welded along a lesser blade's edge. Here the weapon strikes as adamantine, a house rule, since the book gives a part-made edge nothing; the weld line is a weakness a hard parry finds.

weapon.note: a house rule: the book gives a part-made edge no benefit
the weld line
